title.zh: 卷一百九十二 列傳第七十九: 良吏二
title.raw: 卷一百九十二 列傳第七十九: 良吏二 Volume 192 Biographies 79: Virtuous Officials 2

sentences.zh: 耶律伯堅，字壽之，桓州人。

translations.literal: Ye Lü Bojian, styled Shouzhi, was a native of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Lü Bojian, courtesy name Shouzhi, came from Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 氣豪俠，喜與名士遊。

translations.literal: By nature bold and chivalrous, he delighted in associating with eminent scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He had a bold, chivalrous temperament and loved to keep company with distinguished men of letters.

sentences.zh: 用薦舉入官，為工部主事。

translations.literal: Through recommendation he entered official service and became a secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he joined the bureaucracy and was appointed secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 至元九年，轉保定路清苑縣尹。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to be magistrate of Qingyuan County in Baoding Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1272 he was reassigned as magistrate of Qingyuan County on the Baoding circuit.

sentences.zh: 初，安肅州苦徐水之害，訴於大司農司，大司農司欲奪水故道，導水使東。

translations.literal: Initially, Ansuzhou suffered from harm caused by the Xu River and appealed to the Grand Secretariat of Agriculture; the Grand Secretariat wished to seize the river's old course and divert the water eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ansuzhou had been plagued by flooding from the Xu River and petitioned the Grand Secretariat of Agriculture, which planned to seize the river's former channel and divert its waters eastward.

sentences.zh: 東則清苑境也，地勢不利，果導之，則清苑被其害，而水亦必反故道為災。

translations.literal: To the east lay the territory of Qingyuan; the terrain there was unfavorable. If the water were in fact diverted, Qingyuan would suffer the harm, and the water would surely also return to its old course and cause disaster.
translations.idiomatic: East lay Qingyuan territory, where the land lay low and ill-suited to such a change; if the diversion went ahead, Qingyuan would bear the damage, and the water would almost certainly revert to its old bed and bring disaster again.

sentences.zh: 伯堅陳其形勢，圖其利害，要大司農司官及郡守行視可否，事遂得已。

translations.literal: Bojian presented the topography, illustrated the advantages and disadvantages, and demanded that officials of the Grand Secretariat of Agriculture and the prefect go personally to inspect whether it was feasible; the matter was thereby stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Bojian laid out the terrain and spelled out the pros and cons, insisting that Grand Secretariat officials and the prefect come see for themselves whether the scheme would work; the project was dropped.

sentences.zh: 縣西有塘水，溉民田甚廣，勢家據以為磑，民以失利來訴。

translations.literal: West of the county was reservoir water that irrigated the people's fields over a very wide area; powerful families had seized it to operate water mills, and the people came to sue because they had suffered loss.
translations.idiomatic: West of the county lay a reservoir that watered a broad swath of farmland; powerful families had seized it to run mills, and peasants came forward complaining of lost livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 伯堅命毀磑，決其水而注之田，許以溉田之餘月，乃得堰水置磑。

translations.literal: Bojian ordered the mills destroyed, released their water to pour into the fields, and permitted dams and mills only in the months left over after irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the mills torn down, broke their embankments to restore flow to the fields, and allowed mills only in the slack months when irrigation did not require the water.

sentences.zh: 仍以其事聞於省部，著為定制。

translations.literal: He furthermore reported the affair to the provincial authorities, and it was established as a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported the case to provincial headquarters, and it was codified as standing policy.

sentences.zh: 縣居南北之衝，歲為親王大官治供帳於縣西，限以十月成，至明年復撤而新之，吏得併緣侵漁，其費不貲。

translations.literal: The county lay on the thoroughfare between north and south. Every year supply camps for royal princes and high officials were built west of the county, required to be finished by the tenth month, then dismantled the next year and rebuilt anew; clerks were able to seize the opportunity for corruption and extortion, and the costs were countless.
translations.idiomatic: The county stood on the main north-south route, and each year the court had supply encampments built west of town, due by the tenth month—only to be torn down the following year and rebuilt from scratch. Clerks milked the cycle for graft, and the expense was incalculable.

sentences.zh: 伯堅命築公館，以代供帳，其弊遂絕。

translations.literal: Bojian ordered a public guesthouse built to replace the supply camps, and that abuse was thereby ended.
translations.idiomatic: Bojian had a public lodge erected in place of the seasonal camps, and the abuse ceased.

sentences.zh: 凡郡府賦役，於縣有重於他縣者，輒曰：「寧得罪於上，不可得罪於下。

translations.literal: Whenever prefectural levies and corvée fell heavier on the county than on other counties, he would say: "Better to offend those above than to offend those below."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever prefectural taxes or labor fell on his county more heavily than elsewhere, he would declare, "I would rather anger my superiors than wrong the people."

sentences.zh: 」必詣府力爭之。

translations.literal: He invariably went to the prefectural seat and strove with all his might against it.
translations.idiomatic: He would go to the prefecture and fight the assessment tooth and nail.

sentences.zh: 在清苑四年，民親戴之如父母，比去而猶思之，立石頌其德焉。

translations.literal: During four years in Qingyuan, the people cherished and revered him as parents; when he left they still thought of him and erected a stone to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: For four years in Qingyuan the people loved him as they would their own parents; long after he left they still missed him and set up a stone praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 擢為恩州同知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to associate prefect of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy prefect of Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 段直，字正卿，澤州晉城人。

translations.literal: Duan Zhi, styled Zhengqing, was a native of Jincheng in Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhi, courtesy name Zhengqing, was from Jincheng in Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，河北、河東、山東盜賊充斥，直聚其鄉黨族屬，結壘自保。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan, bandits filled Hebei, Hedong, and Shandong; Zhi gathered his townsfolk, clansmen, and kinsmen and built fortifications for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274 banditry engulfed Hebei, Hedong, and Shandong; Duan rallied his neighbors and kinsmen and fortified a stronghold for their protection.

sentences.zh: 世祖命大將略地晉城，直以其眾歸之，幕府承製，署直潞州元帥府右監軍。

translations.literal: The Founder ordered a great general to advance and seize territory around Jincheng; Zhi brought his forces to submit to him. The field headquarters, acting on imperial warrant, appointed Zhi right overseer of the military of the Marshal's Office of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai sent a senior commander to secure Jincheng; Duan brought his followers over and the campaign headquarters, under emergency powers, named him deputy overseer on the Luzhou marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 其後論功行賞，分土世守，命直佩金符，為澤州長官。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when merits were assessed and rewards distributed and fiefs granted for perpetual enfeoffment, Zhi was ordered to wear a gold tally and was made chief administrator of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when rewards were apportioned and hereditary fiefs granted, Duan was given a gold tally and made chief administrator of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 澤民多避兵未還者，直命籍其田廬於親戚鄰人之戶，且約曰：「俟業主至，當析而歸之。

translations.literal: Many of the people of Ze had fled the warfare and not yet returned; Zhi ordered their fields and dwellings registered to the households of relatives and neighbors, with the stipulation: "When the owners return, they shall be apportioned and returned."
translations.idiomatic: Many Ze residents had fled the fighting and not returned; Duan had their land and homes registered to relatives and neighbors on the promise that "when the owners come back, every plot and roof will be returned to them."

sentences.zh: 」逃民聞之，多來還者，命歸其田廬如約，民得安業。

translations.literal: When fugitive peasants heard this, many came back; he ordered their fields and dwellings returned according to the agreement, and the people were able to settle in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees heard of this and streamed home; he restored fields and houses as promised, and the people could live in peace again.

sentences.zh: 素無產者，則出粟賑之；

translations.literal: Those who had long been without livelihood were given grain for relief;
translations.idiomatic: Families with nothing to their name received grain relief;

sentences.zh: 為他郡所俘掠者，出財購之；

translations.literal: those captured and plundered by other prefectures were redeemed with his own funds;
translations.idiomatic: those seized as captives in other districts were bought back at his expense;

sentences.zh: 以兵死而暴露者，收而瘞之。

translations.literal: those who died in war and lay exposed were gathered and buried.
translations.idiomatic: the war dead left unburied on the fields were gathered in and laid to rest.

sentences.zh: 未幾，澤為樂土。

translations.literal: Before long, Ze became a land of peace and joy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ze had become a haven of peace.

sentences.zh: 大修孔子廟，割田千畝，置書萬卷，迎儒士李俊民為師，以招延四方來學者。

translations.literal: He greatly repaired the Temple of Confucius, set aside a thousand mu of fields, stocked ten thousand volumes of books, invited the Confucian scholar Li Junmin as teacher, and thereby drew scholars from all directions who came to study.
translations.idiomatic: He refurbished the Confucian temple on a grand scale, endowed a thousand mu of land, stocked ten thousand books, and brought in Li Junmin as master-teacher to draw students from far and wide.

sentences.zh: 不五六年，學之士子，以通經被選者，百二十有二人。

translations.literal: Within five or six years, among the students at the school, one hundred twenty-two were selected for having mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Within five or six years a hundred twenty-two of his students had passed selection on the strength of classical learning.

sentences.zh: 在官二十年，多有惠政。

translations.literal: During twenty years in office he had many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Over twenty years in office he earned a reputation for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 朝廷特命提舉本州學校事，未拜而卒。

translations.literal: The court specially ordered him to superintend school affairs in his prefecture, but he died before assuming the post.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him to oversee the prefectural schools, but he died before he could take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 諳都剌，字瑞芝，凱烈氏。

translations.literal: Oqatël, styled Ruizhi, was of the Qarluq clan.
translations.idiomatic: Oqatël, courtesy name Ruizhi, was a Qarluq by clan.

sentences.zh: 祖阿思蘭，嘗從大將阿術伐宋，仕至冀寧路達魯花赤，子孫因其名蘭，遂以蘭為氏。

translations.literal: His grandfather Aslan had once followed the great general Aju in the campaign against Song and rose to be darughachi of Jining Circuit; descendants took "Lan" from his name and made it their clan surname.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Aslan had followed the general Aju against the Song and served as darughachi of Jining; later generations took Lan from his name as their family name.

sentences.zh: 諳都剌通經史，兼習諸國語。

translations.literal: Oqatël was versed in the classics and histories and had also studied the various national languages.
translations.idiomatic: Oqatël was steeped in the classics and histories and fluent in several court languages besides.

sentences.zh: 成宗時，為翰林院札爾里赤，職書制誥。

translations.literal: During the reign of Chengzong he was jarlichi of the Hanlin Academy, his duty being to draft imperial patents and edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Temür (Chengzong) he served as the Hanlin Academy's jarlichi, responsible for drafting patents and edicts.

sentences.zh: 會有旨命書籓王添力聖旨，諳都剌曰：「此旨非惟有虧國體，行且為民殃矣。

translations.literal: Once there was an imperial order to draft an edict for the frontier prince Tianli; Oqatël said: "This edict will not only damage the dignity of the state—it will soon bring calamity upon the people as well."
translations.idiomatic: Once the court ordered him to draft an edict for the frontier prince Tianli; Oqatël objected: "Such a patent would disgrace the realm and bring ruin on the people besides."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之，謂近臣曰：「小吏如此，真難得也。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he said to his close attendants: "For a petty clerk to be like this is truly rare."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, hearing of it, told his intimates, "For a junior clerk to show such spirit—that is truly exceptional."

sentences.zh: 」事乃止。

translations.literal: The matter was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The order was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 尋授應奉翰林文字，凡蒙古傳記，多所校正。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed editorial drafter in the Hanlin Academy; all Mongolian biographies he largely corrected.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Hanlin editorial drafter and corrected many errors in Mongolian historical texts.

sentences.zh: 升待制。

translations.literal: He was promoted to academician-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 時方選守令，除遼州達魯花赤，以最聞，賜上尊名幣，除集賢直學士。

translations.literal: When prefects and magistrates were being selected, he was appointed darughachi of Liaozhou. Known as outstanding, he was granted fine wine and honorary gifts, and appointed direct scholar of the Jixian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During a round of provincial appointments he was named darughachi of Liaozhou; his excellence won imperial wine and honors, and he was made direct scholar of the Jixian Academy.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，遷襄陽路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was transferred to be darughachi of Xiangyang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1330 he was transferred to serve as darughachi of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 山西大饑，河南行省恐流民入境為變，檄守武關，諳都剌驗其良民，輒聽其度關。

translations.literal: Shanxi suffered a great famine; the Henan Branch Secretariat feared that displaced people entering the province might cause unrest and ordered Wuguan Pass held; Oqatël examined those who were honest common folk and always permitted them to cross.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanxi was struck by famine the Henan secretariat feared unrest from refugees and sealed Wuguan Pass; Oqatël screened peaceful families and let them through.

sentences.zh: 吏曰：「得無違上命乎？

translations.literal: A clerk said: "Will this not violate the superior's order?"
translations.idiomatic: A clerk asked, "Are you not defying headquarters?"

sentences.zh: 」諳都剌曰：「吾防奸耳，非仇良民也，可不開其生路耶！

translations.literal: Oqatël said: "I guard against villains—I do not make enemies of honest people. How could I fail to open a path for them to live?"
translations.idiomatic: Oqatël replied, "I am guarding against rogues, not hounding honest folk—should I not leave them a way to survive?"

sentences.zh: 」既又煮粥以食之，所活數万人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again cooked porridge to feed them, and the number he saved was in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He also had gruel cooked for them, saving tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 又城臨漢水，歲有水患，為築堤城外，遂以無虞。

translations.literal: Moreover, the city lay along the Han River and every year suffered flooding; he built dikes outside the walls, and thereafter there was no worry.
translations.idiomatic: The city fronted the Han, which flooded yearly; he built outer embankments and the town was thereafter secure.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，除益都路總管。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong he was appointed chief administrator of Yidu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1334 he was made chief administrator of Yidu circuit.

sentences.zh: 俗頗悍黠，而諳都剌務興學校，以平易治之。

translations.literal: The customs were rather fierce and cunning, yet Oqatël devoted himself to establishing schools and governed with simplicity and leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The region was rough and shrewd, but Oqatël promoted schools and governed with plain, gentle fairness.

sentences.zh: 有上馬賊白晝劫人，久不能捕，諳都剌生擒之，其黨賂宣慰使羅鍋，誣以枉勘，縱其賊。

translations.literal: There were mounted bandits who robbed people in broad daylight and could not be captured for a long time; Oqatël seized them alive. Their gang bribed the Pacification Commissioner Luo Guo and falsely accused him of wrongful investigation, and the bandits were released.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted robbers had terrorized the roads by day for years without capture; Oqatël took them alive. Their associates bribed Pacification Commissioner Luo Guo to accuse him of wrongful prosecution and the thieves walked free.

sentences.zh: 已而賊劫河間，復被獲，乃盡輸其情，而諳都剌之誣始白，俾再任一考。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits raided Hejian and were captured again; they then fully confessed the facts, and Oqatël's false accusation was at last cleared; he was allowed to serve another evaluation term.
translations.idiomatic: Later the same band struck Hejian and were caught again; they confessed everything, clearing Oqatël's name and earning him another term in office.

sentences.zh: 親王買奴鎮益都，其府屬病民，諳都剌裁抑之，民以無擾。

translations.literal: Prince Mainu was stationed in Yidu; his household staff oppressed the people; Oqatël restrained them, and the people were thus undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mainu was posted to Yidu with a household staff that harassed the people; Oqatël curbed them and peace returned.

sentences.zh: 至正六年卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhizheng he died at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1346 at seventy.

sentences.zh: 子燮徹堅，同知新喻州事，以孝稱。

translations.literal: His son Seyiqi, associate prefect of Xinyu, was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His son Seyiqi, deputy prefect of Xinyu, was renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 楊景行，字賢可，吉安太和州人。

translations.literal: Yang Jingxing, styled Xiankai, was a native of Taihe Prefecture in Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jingxing, courtesy name Xiankai, was from Taihe in Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 登延祐二年進士第，授贛州路會昌州判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yanyou and was appointed assistant prefect of Huichang Subprefecture in Ganzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in 1315 and was appointed assistant prefect of Huichang in Ganzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 會昌民素不知井飲，汲於河流，故多疾癘；

translations.literal: The people of Huichang had long been unaccustomed to drinking from wells and drew water from the river, so there were many epidemics;
translations.idiomatic: Huichang folk had never drawn drinking water from wells and took it from the river instead, so epidemics were common;

sentences.zh: 不知陶瓦，以茅覆屋，故多火災。

translations.literal: they did not know pottery tiles and roofed their houses with thatch, so there were many fires.
translations.idiomatic: they knew nothing of tile and thatched their roofs, so fires were frequent.

sentences.zh: 景行教民穿井以飲，陶瓦以代茅茨，民始免於疾癘火災。

translations.literal: Jingxing taught the people to dig wells for drinking and to use pottery tiles in place of thatch; the people were thereby freed from epidemics and fires.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxing taught them to sink wells for drinking water and to roof with tile instead of thatch, and the district was finally spared epidemics and conflagrations.

sentences.zh: 豪民十人，號十虎，干政害民，悉捕置之法。

translations.literal: Ten powerful men, called the Ten Tigers, interfered in government and harmed the people; he arrested them all and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Ten local strongmen known as the Ten Tigers had meddled in government and preyed on the people; he arrested them all and punished them to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 乃創學舍，禮師儒，勸民斥腴田以膳士，弦誦之聲遂盛。

translations.literal: He then founded a schoolhouse, honored Confucian teachers, and urged the people to devote fertile fields to feed scholars; the sound of recitation and study thereupon flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a school, honored Confucian masters, and urged families to set aside fertile land to support students; soon the district rang with study.

sentences.zh: 調永新州判官，奉郡府命，核民田租，除剷宿弊，姦欺不容，細民賴焉。

translations.literal: Transferred to be assistant prefect of Yongxin, he carried out the prefectural command to audit the people's land tax, uprooted longstanding abuses, tolerated no fraud, and humble folk relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yongxin as assistant prefect, he audited land taxes on prefectural orders, uprooted entrenched abuses, brooked no fraud, and ordinary people came to depend on him.

sentences.zh: 改江西行省照磨，轉撫州路宜黃縣尹，理白冤獄之不決者數十事。

translations.literal: He was changed to archival reviewer of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, then transferred to be magistrate of Yihuang County in Fuzhou Circuit, and cleared dozens of wrongful cases that had gone unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: He became archival reviewer for the Jiangxi secretariat, then magistrate of Yihuang in Fuzhou circuit, and cleared dozens of long-stalled wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 升撫州路總管府推官，發擿姦伏，郡無冤獄。

translations.literal: Promoted to investigating officer of the Fuzhou Circuit chief administrator's office, he exposed hidden wrongdoing, and the prefecture had no wrongful imprisonments.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to investigating officer for Fuzhou circuit, he exposed hidden crimes until the prefecture held no wrongful cases.

sentences.zh: 金溪縣民陶甲，厚積而凶險，嘗屢誣陷其縣長吏罷去之，由是官吏畏其人，不敢詰治，陶遂暴橫於一郡。

translations.literal: A man of Jinxi County named Tao Jia, wealthy and fierce, had repeatedly framed and driven out his county magistrates; thereafter officials feared him and dared not investigate, and Tao came to run rampant through the whole prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Jia of Jinxi was rich, brutal, and had repeatedly framed county magistrates until they were removed; officials thereafter feared him and dared not prosecute, and Tao tyrannized the whole prefecture.

sentences.zh: 景行至，以法痛繩之，徙五百里外。

translations.literal: When Jingxing arrived, he punished him severely according to law and exiled him five hundred li away.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxing took office he punished Tao to the full letter of the law and exiled him five hundred li distant.

sentences.zh: 金溪豪僧云住，發人塚墓取財物，事覺，官吏受賄，緩其獄，景行急按之，僧以賄動之，不聽，乃賂當道者，以危語撼之，一不顧，卒治之如法。

translations.literal: A powerful monk of Jinxi named Yunzhu had opened people's tombs and graves to take valuables; when the affair came to light, officials took bribes and slowed his case. Jingxing pressed the investigation urgently; the monk tried to move him with bribes, but he would not listen. The monk then bribed those in power and used threatening words to shake him, but Jingxing paid no heed and in the end punished him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful Jinxi monk named Yunzhu had been robbing graves; when the crime surfaced, officials took bribes and stalled the case. Jingxing pressed the prosecution; the monk tried bribery, then bribed higher authorities and threatened him—Jingxing ignored it all and punished him by law.

sentences.zh: 由是豪猾屏跡，良民獲安。

translations.literal: Thereby the powerful and cunning withdrew from sight, and honest people gained peace.
translations.idiomatic: The bullies vanished from sight and honest folk lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 轉湖州路歸安縣尹，奉行省命，理荒田租，民無欺弊。

translations.literal: Transferred to be magistrate of Gui'an County in Huzhou Circuit, he carried out the provincial command to settle tax on abandoned fields, and the people suffered no fraud or abuse.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Gui'an in Huzhou he carried out provincial orders to settle tax on abandoned land, and the people were spared fraud and abuse.

sentences.zh: 景行所歷州縣，皆有惠政；

translations.literal: In every prefecture and county Jingxing passed through, he had benevolent policies;
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held Jingxing left benevolent policies behind;

sentences.zh: 所去，民皆立石頌之。

translations.literal: wherever he left, the people all erected stones to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: and wherever he moved on, the people set up stones in his praise.

sentences.zh: 以翰林待制、朝列大夫致仕，年七十四卒。

translations.literal: He retired with the titles Hanlin academician-in-waiting and Grand Master of the Court, and died at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Hanlin academician and Grand Master of the Court and died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 林興祖，字宗起，福州羅源人。

translations.literal: Lin Xingzu, styled Zongqi, was a native of Luoyuan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xingzu, courtesy name Zongqi, was from Luoyuan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，登進士第，授承事郎、同知黃岩州事，三遷而知鉛山州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Gentleman for Managing Affairs and associate prefect of Huangyan, and after three promotions became prefect of Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in 1322, was appointed deputy prefect of Huangyan, and after three promotions became prefect of Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 鉛山素多造偽鈔者，豪民吳友文為之魁，遠至江淮、燕薊，莫不行使。

translations.literal: Qianshan had long had many makers of counterfeit paper money; the powerful man Wu Youwen was their leader, and as far as the Jiang-Huai region and Yan-Ji, none failed to circulate their notes.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshan had long been notorious for counterfeit banknotes, with the magnate Wu Youwen as ringleader; his notes circulated as far as the Jiang-Huai and Yan-Ji regions.

sentences.zh: 友文姦黠悍鷙，因偽造致富，乃分遣惡少四五十人，為吏於有司，伺有欲告之者，輒先事戕之，前後殺人甚眾，奪人妻女十一人為妾，民罹其害，銜冤不敢訴者十餘年。

translations.literal: Youwen was cunning, fierce, and brutal; through counterfeiting he grew rich, then sent out forty or fifty ruffians to serve as clerks in government offices. When anyone wished to report him, they would kill him first; before and after they killed very many people. He seized eleven men's wives and daughters as concubines. The people suffered his harm and bore grievances but dared not sue for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen was cunning, fierce, and brutal; counterfeiting made him rich, and he planted forty or fifty thugs as clerks in government offices to murder anyone who tried to inform before they could act—killing many over the years and seizing eleven women as concubines. For more than a decade the people suffered in silence, too afraid to sue.

sentences.zh: 興祖至官，曰：「此害不除，何以牧民！

translations.literal: When Xingzu took office he said: "If this harm is not removed, how can I govern the people!"
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Xingzu declared, "If this scourge is not uprooted, how can I govern the people!"

sentences.zh: 」即張榜禁偽造者，且立賞募民首告。

translations.literal: He immediately posted proclamations forbidding counterfeiters and offered rewards to recruit people to report first.
translations.idiomatic: He posted notices forbidding counterfeiting and offered rewards for informants.

sentences.zh: 俄有告者至，佯以不實斥去；

translations.literal: Soon an informant came; he pretended to dismiss him as untrue;
translations.idiomatic: When an informant soon appeared, he pretended to dismiss the charge as false;

sentences.zh: 又有告獲偽造二人並贓者，乃鞫之，款成。

translations.literal: then another report came of two counterfeiters captured with the evidence; he interrogated them and the confession was complete.
translations.idiomatic: then came word that two counterfeiters had been seized with the evidence; he interrogated them until they confessed fully.

sentences.zh: 友文自至官，為之營救，興祖命並執之。

translations.literal: Youwen came in person to the office to rescue them; Xingzu ordered him seized as well.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen came to the yamen in person to intervene; Xingzu ordered him arrested too.

sentences.zh: 須臾，來訴友文者百餘人，擇其重罪一二事鞫之，獄立具，逮捕其黨二百餘人，悉置之法。

translations.literal: In no time more than a hundred people came to accuse Youwen; he selected one or two of the gravest crimes for interrogation, the case was immediately complete, and more than two hundred of his gang were arrested and all punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Within moments more than a hundred accusers came forward; he tried one or two of the gravest charges, the case was complete at once, and over two hundred accomplices were arrested and punished.

sentences.zh: 民害既去，政聲籍甚。

translations.literal: Once the people's harm was removed, his reputation for governance became widely known.
translations.idiomatic: With the scourge gone, his reputation for good government spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 江浙行省丞相別兒怯不花薦諸朝，升南陽知府，改建德路同知，俱未任。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat chancellor Bayiqinbuqa recommended him to the court; he was promoted to prefect of Nanyang and then associate prefect of Jiande Circuit, but took neither post.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Zhe chancellor Bayiqinbuqa recommended him to court; he was promoted to prefect of Nanyang and then deputy prefect of Jiande, but never took either post.

sentences.zh: 至正八年，特旨遷為道州路總管，行至城外，撞賊已迫其後，相去僅二十里。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhizheng he was specially ordered transferred to be chief administrator of Daozhou Circuit. When he reached outside the city walls, bandits were already pressing behind him, only twenty li away.
translations.idiomatic: In 1348 he was specially appointed chief administrator of Daozhou; as he reached the suburbs, rebel forces were only twenty li behind.

sentences.zh: 時湖南副使哈剌帖木兒屯兵城外，聞賊至，以乏軍需，欲退兵，興祖聞，即夜詣說留之。

translations.literal: At the time the Hunan vice commissioner Qaratemür was encamped outside the city; hearing the bandits were coming and lacking military supplies, he wished to withdraw his troops. When Xingzu heard of it, he went that night to persuade him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan vice commissioner Qaratemür was camped outside the walls; hearing the rebels approach and lacking supplies, he meant to withdraw. Xingzu went to him that night and persuaded him to stand firm.

sentences.zh: 哈剌帖木兒曰：「明日得鈔五千錠、桐盾五百，乃可破賊。

translations.literal: Qaratemür said: "Tomorrow, if I obtain five thousand ingots of paper money and five hundred paulownia shields, then I can defeat the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Qaratemür said, "Give me five thousand ingots of paper money and five hundred paulownia shields by tomorrow, and I can break the rebels."

sentences.zh: 」興祖許之。

translations.literal: Xingzu promised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu agreed.

sentences.zh: 明日甫入城視事，即以恩信勸諭鹽商，貸鈔五千錠，且取郡樓舊桐板為盾，日中皆備。

translations.literal: The next day, as soon as he entered the city to take up his duties, he used sincerity and trust to persuade the salt merchants to lend five thousand ingots of paper money, and took old paulownia boards from the prefectural tower for shields; by midday all was ready.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning, as soon as he entered the city to take office, he persuaded salt merchants on trust to lend five thousand ingots and had old paulownia boards from the city tower fashioned into shields; everything was ready by noon.

sentences.zh: 哈剌帖木兒得鈔、盾，大喜，遂留，為御賊計。

translations.literal: Qaratemür received the money and shields and was greatly pleased; he then stayed and made plans to resist the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Qaratemür received the money and shields, was delighted, and stayed to plan the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊聞新總管至，一日具五百盾，以為大軍且至，中夕遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits heard the new chief administrator had arrived and that five hundred shields had been prepared in a single day; they thought a great army was about to come and fled at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels heard a new chief administrator had arrived and that five hundred shields had been readied in a day; believing a large army was coming, they fled at midnight.

sentences.zh: 永明縣洞徭屢竊發為民害，興祖以手榜諭之。

translations.literal: The cave Yao of Yongming County repeatedly rose in theft and harmed the people; Xingzu addressed them with a handwritten proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: The cave Yao of Yongming had repeatedly raided the countryside; Xingzu addressed them with a handwritten proclamation.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「林總管廉而愛民，不可犯也。

translations.literal: They all said: "Prefect Lin is incorrupt and loves the people—he must not be offended."
translations.idiomatic: They all said, "Prefect Lin is honest and loves the people—we must not offend him."

sentences.zh: 」三年不入境。

translations.literal: For three years they did not enter the district.
translations.idiomatic: For three years they did not cross the border.

sentences.zh: 春旱，蟲食麥苗，興祖為文禱之，大雨三日，蟲死而麥稔。

translations.literal: In spring there was drought and insects ate the wheat seedlings; Xingzu composed a prayer text, and heavy rain fell for three days; the insects died and the wheat ripened.
translations.idiomatic: A spring drought brought locusts on the wheat; Xingzu wrote a prayer, rain fell for three days, the pests died, and the crop ripened.

sentences.zh: 已而罷興作，賑貧乏，輕徭薄斂，郡中大治，憲司考課，以道州為最。

translations.literal: Thereafter he halted extravagant construction, relieved the poor, lightened corvée and reduced levies; the prefecture was greatly well governed, and in the surveillance commission's evaluation Daozhou ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: He halted wasteful public works, relieved the poor, lightened labor and tax burdens, and brought the prefecture to good order; in the surveillance commission's review Daozhou ranked first.

sentences.zh: 以年老致仕，終於家。

translations.literal: He retired on account of old age and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He retired in old age and died at home.

sentences.zh: 觀音奴，字志能，唐兀人氏，居新州。

translations.literal: Guanyin Nu, styled Zhineng, was of the Tangut people and lived in Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guanyin Nu, courtesy name Zhineng, was a Tangut who lived in Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 登泰定四年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Taiding.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in 1327.

sentences.zh: 由戶部主事，再轉而知歸德府。

translations.literal: From secretary in the Ministry of Revenue he was twice transferred to become prefect of Guide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: From a post as secretary in the Ministry of Revenue he was twice promoted until he became prefect of Guide.

sentences.zh: 廉明剛斷，發擿如神。

translations.literal: Incorrupt, clear-sighted, and resolute in judgment, he exposed wrongdoing as if by divine insight.
translations.idiomatic: Honest, clear-sighted, and firm in judgment, he uncovered wrongdoing with uncanny precision.

sentences.zh: 民有銜冤不直者，雖數十年前事，皆千里奔走來訴，觀音奴立為剖決，旬日悉清。

translations.literal: When the people bore grievances that had not been righted, even affairs from decades before, they all ran a thousand li to come and plead; Guanyin Nu immediately judged and decided for them, and within ten days all was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: People with old wrongs unresolved—even cases from decades past—would travel a thousand li to seek justice; Guanyin Nu heard them at once, and within ten days every backlog was cleared.

sentences.zh: 彰德富商任甲，抵睢陽，驢斃，令郄乙剖之，任以怒毆郄，經宿而死。

translations.literal: A wealthy merchant of Zhangde named Ren Jia reached Suiyang; his donkey died, and he ordered Qie Yi to butcher it. Ren in anger beat Qie, and after a night Qie died.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Jia, a rich merchant from Zhangde, reached Suiyang; when his donkey died he ordered Qie Yi to butcher it, then beat Qie in a rage until he died overnight.

sentences.zh: 郄有妻王氏、妾孫氏，孫訴於官，官吏納任賄，謂郄非傷死，反抵孫罪，置之獄。

translations.literal: Qie had a wife, Lady Wang, and a concubine, Lady Sun. Lady Sun sued at court; officials took bribes from Ren and said Qie had not died from injury, but instead charged Lady Sun with a crime and put her in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Qie's wife Wang and concubine Sun sued; officials took Ren's bribes, ruled Qie had not died from beating, charged Sun instead, and jailed her.

sentences.zh: 王來訴冤，觀音奴立破械出孫於獄，呼府胥語之曰：「吾為文具香幣，若為吾以郄事禱諸城隍神，令神顯於吾。

translations.literal: Wang came to plead her grievance; Guanyin Nu immediately broke the fetters and released Sun from prison, summoned a prefectural clerk, and told him: "I will prepare the documents, incense, and offerings; you go pray to the City God about Qie's case on my behalf, and let the god reveal the truth to me."
translations.idiomatic: Wang came to plead her case; Guanyin Nu freed Sun from prison at once, called a clerk, and said, "Prepare the papers, incense, and offerings—you will pray to the City God about Qie's death and have the god reveal the truth to me."

sentences.zh: 」有睢陽小吏，亦預郄事，畏觀音奴嚴明，且懼神顯其事，乃以任所賂鈔陳首曰：「郄實傷死，任賂上下匿其實，吾亦得賂，敢以首。

translations.literal: A petty clerk of Suiyang who had also been involved in Qie's case, fearing Guanyin Nu's severity and dreading that the god would reveal the affair, brought forward the paper money Ren had bribed him with and confessed: "Qie truly died from injury; Ren bribed officials high and low to conceal the facts, and I too received a bribe—I dare to inform."
translations.idiomatic: A Suiyang clerk involved in the case, fearing Guanyin Nu's rigor and divine exposure, produced Ren's bribe money and confessed: "Qie truly died from the beating; Ren bribed officials to cover it up, and I took a bribe too—I come to inform."

sentences.zh: 」於是罪任商而釋孫妾。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ren the merchant was punished and the concubine Sun was released.
translations.idiomatic: Ren was punished and Sun was freed.

sentences.zh: 寧陵豪民楊甲，夙嗜王乙田三頃，不能得。

translations.literal: A powerful man of Ningling named Yang Jia had long coveted three qing of Wang Yi's fields but could not obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jia, a Ningling magnate, had long coveted three qing of Wang Yi's land but could not get them.

sentences.zh: 值王以飢攜其妻就食淮南，而王得疾死，其妻還，則田為楊據矣。

translations.literal: When Wang, because of famine, took his wife to seek food in Huainan, Wang fell ill and died; when his wife returned, the fields were already held by Yang.
translations.idiomatic: When famine drove Wang and his wife to Huainan for food, Wang fell ill and died; when his wife returned, Yang already held the fields.

sentences.zh: 王妻訴之官，楊行賄，偽作文憑，曰：「王在時已售我。

translations.literal: Wang's wife sued at court; Yang gave bribes and forged a written deed, saying: "When Wang was alive he had already sold to me."
translations.idiomatic: Wang's wife sued; Yang bribed officials and forged a deed claiming Wang had sold him the land while alive.

sentences.zh: 」觀音奴令王妻挽楊，同就崔府君神祠質之。

translations.literal: Guanyin Nu ordered Wang's wife to take Yang by the arm and go together to the shrine of Lord Cui to confront the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Guanyin Nu had Wang's wife take Yang to the shrine of Lord Cui to settle the matter before the god.

sentences.zh: 楊懼神之靈，先期以羊酒浼巫囑神勿洩其事，及王與楊詣祠質之，果無所顯明。

translations.literal: Yang feared the god's power; beforehand he used sheep and wine to beg the shaman to ask the god not to reveal the affair. When Wang and Yang went to the shrine to confront the matter, indeed nothing was revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the god, Yang bribed the shaman with sheep and wine to ask the deity to stay silent; when Wang and Yang went to the shrine, nothing was revealed.

sentences.zh: 觀音奴疑之，召巫詰問，巫吐其實曰：「楊以羊酒浼我囑神曰：'我實據王田，幸神勿洩也。

translations.literal: Guanyin Nu grew suspicious and summoned the shaman for interrogation; the shaman confessed the truth, saying: "Yang used sheep and wine to beg me to tell the god: 'I have in fact seized Wang's fields—may the god not reveal it.'"
translations.idiomatic: Guanyin Nu grew suspicious and questioned the shaman, who confessed: "Yang gave me sheep and wine and asked the god not to reveal that he had seized Wang's land."

sentences.zh: '」觀音奴因訊得其實，坐楊罪，歸其田王氏，責神而撤其祠。

translations.literal: Guanyin Nu thereby interrogated and obtained the truth, punished Yang, returned the fields to the Wang family, rebuked the god, and demolished the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Guanyin Nu got the truth, punished Yang, restored the land to the Wangs, rebuked the shrine, and had it torn down.

sentences.zh: 亳州有蝗食民禾，觀音奴以事至亳，民以蝗訴，立取蝗向天祝之，以水研碎而飲，是歲蝗不為災。

translations.literal: In Bozhou locusts were eating the people's grain; Guanyin Nu came to Bozhou on business, and the people complained of the locusts. He immediately took locusts, prayed to Heaven over them, ground them with water and drank them, and that year the locusts did not become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When locusts devoured the crops in Bozhou, Guanyin Nu on official business took locusts, prayed heavenward, ground them in water and drank the mixture—and that year the plague did no harm.

sentences.zh: 後升為都水監官。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to an office in the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to an office in the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 周自強，字剛善，臨江路新喻州人。

translations.literal: Zhou Ziqiang, styled Gangshan, was a native of Xinyu Prefecture in Linjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ziqiang, courtesy name Gangshan, was from Xinyu in Linjiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 好學能文，練於吏事，以文法推擇為吏。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled in writing, practiced in clerical affairs, and was selected as a clerk through literary and legal examination.
translations.idiomatic: A devoted student and capable writer, skilled in administrative work, he was selected as a clerk through competitive examination.

sentences.zh: 泰定間，廣西洞徭反，自強往見徭酋，說以禍福，中其要害，徭酋立為罷兵，貢方物，納款請命。

translations.literal: During the Taiding era the cave Yao of Guangxi rebelled; Ziqiang went to see the Yao chieftains and spoke to them of fortune and calamity, striking their vital point; the chieftains immediately ceased hostilities, presented local products, and submitted in surrender to request orders.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiding era the Guangxi cave Yao rebelled; Ziqiang went to their chiefs, spoke of reward and ruin, and hit their weak point; they at once laid down arms, sent tribute, and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 事聞於朝，特旨超授廣西兩江道宣慰司都事。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported to court, he was specially ordered promoted by exception to chief secretary of the Guangxi Liangjiang Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The court heard of it and specially promoted him to chief secretary of the Guangxi Liangjiang Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 轉饒州路經歷，遷婺州路義烏縣尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be intendant of Raozhou Circuit and promoted to magistrate of Yiwu County in Wuzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became intendant of Raozhou circuit and then magistrate of Yiwu in Wuzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 周知民情，而性度寬厚，不為刻深。

translations.literal: He thoroughly understood the people's sentiments, yet his nature was generous and he was not harsh or severe.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the people's hearts well, yet governed with generous temper and without harshness.

sentences.zh: 民有以爭訟訴於庭者，一見即能知其曲直，然未遽加以刑責，必取經典中語，反覆開譬之，令其誦讀講解。

translations.literal: When the people brought lawsuits to court, at a single glance he could know right and wrong, yet he did not immediately impose punishment; he always took passages from the classics, repeatedly enlightened them, and made them recite and explain.
translations.idiomatic: When litigants came to court he could see right and wrong at a glance, yet he never rushed to punish; he quoted the classics, explained them patiently, and made the parties recite and discuss them.

sentences.zh: 若能悔悟首實，則原其罪；

translations.literal: if they could repent and confess truthfully, he pardoned their crime;
translations.idiomatic: If they repented and confessed, he pardoned them;

sentences.zh: 若迷謬怙惡不悛，然後繩之以法不少貸。

translations.literal: if they were deluded, clung to evil, and would not reform, only then did he bind them with the law without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: only if they persisted in error and clung to evil did he apply the law without mercy.

sentences.zh: 民畏且愛，獄訟頓息。

translations.literal: The people both feared and loved him, and litigation quickly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The people feared and loved him alike, and lawsuits dwindled away.

sentences.zh: 民間田稅之籍多失實，以故差徭不平，自強出令履畝核之，民不能欺，文簿井井可考，於是賦役平均，貧富樂業。

translations.literal: The people's registers of field tax were mostly inaccurate, so corvée and levies were unequal; Ziqiang issued orders to measure fields foot by foot and verify them; the people could not deceive him, the documents were orderly and verifiable, and thereby taxes and labor were equalized and rich and poor alike found contentment in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Land-tax registers were often false, skewing labor and levies; Ziqiang ordered fields measured plot by plot so no one could cheat; the records became reliable, taxes and corvée were fair, and rich and poor alike prospered.

sentences.zh: 其聽訟決獄，物無遁情，黠吏欲以片言欺惑之不可得。

translations.literal: In hearing cases and judging prisons, nothing escaped his knowledge; crafty clerks who wished to deceive him with a single phrase could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In court nothing escaped him; no clever clerk could fool him with a word.

sentences.zh: 由是政治大行，聲譽籍甚。

translations.literal: Thereby good government flourished greatly and his reputation became widely known.
translations.idiomatic: Good government flourished and his fame spread far.

sentences.zh: 部使者數以廉能舉於朝，選授撫州路金溪縣尹，階奉議大夫，政績愈著。

translations.literal: Department envoys repeatedly recommended his integrity and ability to the court; he was selected and appointed magistrate of Jinxi County in Fuzhou Circuit, with the rank of Grand Master of Discussion, and his administrative achievements grew still more notable.
translations.idiomatic: Department inspectors repeatedly recommended him to court; he was appointed magistrate of Jinxi in Fuzhou with the rank of Grand Master of Discussion, and his achievements grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 以亞中大夫、江州路總管致仕。

translations.literal: He retired with the titles Subordinate Grand Master of the Palace and chief administrator of Jiangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Subordinate Grand Master and former chief administrator of Jiangzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 白景亮，字明甫，南陽人。

translations.literal: Bai Jingliang, styled Mingfu, was a native of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Jingliang, courtesy name Mingfu, was from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 明法律，善書算。

translations.literal: He understood laws and was skilled in writing and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered law and excelled at accounts and documents.

sentences.zh: 由征東行省譯史有勞，超遷南恩知州，升沔陽府尹，奏最於朝，特授衢州路總管。

translations.literal: Through meritorious service as translator-clerk in the Eastern Campaign Branch Secretariat, he was promoted by exception to prefect of Nan'en, then raised to prefect of Mianyang, reported top performance to the court, and was specially appointed chief administrator of Quzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: For service as a translator-clerk on the eastern campaign he was promoted to prefect of Nan'en, then Mianyang; after reporting top marks to court he was specially made chief administrator of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，為郡者於民間徭役，不盡校​​田畝以為則，吏得併緣高下其手，富民或優有餘力，而貧弱不能勝者，多至破產失業。

translations.literal: Previously, those who governed prefectures, in the people's corvée and labor service, did not fully verify field acreage as the standard; clerks were able to seize the opportunity to raise or lower amounts at will; wealthy households might enjoy surplus strength, while the poor and weak who could not bear the burden often came to bankruptcy and loss of livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier prefects had not fully verified acreage when assigning corvée, so clerks manipulated the figures; the rich often had spare capacity while the poor were ruined and driven from their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 景亮深知其弊，乃始核驗田畝以均之，役之輕重，一視田之多寡，大小家各使得宜，咸便安之，由是民不勞而事易集，他郡邑皆取以為法。

translations.literal: Jingliang deeply understood this abuse and therefore began to verify field acreage to equalize burdens; the weight of labor service was wholly determined by the amount of land, and large and small households each obtained what was fitting; all found it convenient and settled; thereby the people were not overburdened and affairs were easily accomplished, and other prefectures and counties all took this as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Jingliang saw the abuse clearly and began verifying acreage to spread the burden fairly; labor was scaled strictly to landholding, large and small households alike were treated justly, the people were not overtaxed, work was easily done, and other districts took his method as their model.

sentences.zh: 郡學之政久弛，從祀諸賢無塑像，諸生無廩膳，祭服樂器有缺，景亮皆為備之，儒風大振，縉紳稱頌焉。

translations.literal: The administration of the prefectural school had long been lax; the worthies in the accompanying sacrifices had no statues; students had no stipends; sacrificial robes and musical instruments were lacking—Jingliang provided all of these, Confucian culture flourished greatly, and gentry and officials praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural school had long declined—sage statues were missing, students had no stipends, ritual robes and instruments were lacking; Jingliang supplied them all, learning revived, and the gentry praised him.

sentences.zh: 景亮性廉介勤苦，自奉甚薄，妻尤儉約，惟以脫粟對飯而已。

translations.literal: Jingliang's nature was incorrupt, upright, diligent, and frugal; his own maintenance was very spare, and his wife was especially economical—they had only husked grain with rice for meals.
translations.idiomatic: Jingliang was honest, upright, and frugal; he lived very simply, and his wife was still more austere—they ate only plain grain with rice.

sentences.zh: 部使者嘗上其事，特詔褒美，賜以宮錦，改授台州路總管。

translations.literal: A department envoy once reported this affair to the throne; an imperial edict specially praised and commended him, granted palace brocade, and transferred him to be chief administrator of Taizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: A department inspector reported his conduct to court; the emperor specially commended him, granted palace brocade, and transferred him to chief administrator of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 王艮，字止善，紹興諸暨人。

translations.literal: Wang Gen, styled Zhishan, was a native of Zhuji in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gen, courtesy name Zhishan, was from Zhuji in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 尚氣節，讀書務明理以致用，不苟事言說。

translations.literal: He valued integrity and moral courage; in reading he strove to clarify principle for practical use and did not casually engage in empty discourse.
translations.idiomatic: He prized integrity; he read to grasp principle for practical use and disdained empty talk.

sentences.zh: 淮東廉訪司辟為書吏，遷淮西。

translations.literal: The Huaidong Surveillance Commission recruited him as a clerical secretary; he was transferred to Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: The Huaidong surveillance commission recruited him as a clerk; he was transferred to Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 會例革南士，就為吏於兩淮都轉運鹽使司，以歲月及格，授廬州錄事判官。

translations.literal: When regulations abolished southern scholars' posts, he became a clerk in the Lianghuai Salt Transport Commission; when his years of service qualified him, he was appointed recording secretary and assistant judge of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When southern scholars were barred from office by regulation, he served as a clerk in the Lianghuai Salt Transport Commission and, when seniority qualified him, was appointed recording secretary and assistant judge of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮東宣慰司辟為令史，以廉能稱。

translations.literal: The Huaidong Pacification Commission recruited him as a chief clerk, and he was known for integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: The Huaidong Pacification Commission recruited him as chief clerk, and he was known for integrity and ability.

sentences.zh: 再調峽州總管府知事，又辟江浙行省掾史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to be administrative secretary of the Xizhou chief administrator's office, and again recruited as a secretarial clerk of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administrative secretary in Xizhou and then recruited as a clerk for the Jiang-Zhe secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷復立諸市舶司，艮從省官至泉州，建言：「若買舊有之船以付舶商，則費省而工易集，且可絕官吏侵欺掊克之弊。

translations.literal: When the court re-established the maritime trade superintendencies, Gen followed the provincial officials to Quanzhou and proposed: "If existing ships are purchased and entrusted to merchant fleets, expense will be saved and labor easily gathered, and the abuse of officials' encroachment, fraud, and extortion can be ended."
translations.idiomatic: When the court restored the maritime trade offices, Gen went with provincial officials to Quanzhou and proposed buying existing vessels for merchant fleets—saving expense, easing assembly, and ending official graft and extortion.

sentences.zh: 」中書省報如艮言。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat replied agreeing with Gen's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Secretariat approved Gen's proposal.

sentences.zh: 凡為船六宗，省官錢五十餘萬緡。

translations.literal: In all six ships were built, saving more than five hundred thousand strings of official money.
translations.idiomatic: Six ships were built in all, saving more than five hundred thousand strings of official funds.

sentences.zh: 歷建德縣尹，除兩浙都轉運鹽使司經歷。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Jiande County and was appointed intendant of the Liang-Zhe Salt Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Jiande and was appointed intendant of the Liang-Zhe Salt Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 紹興路總管王克敬，以計口食鹽不便，嘗言於，行省，未報，而克敬為轉運使，集議欲稍損其額，以紓民力。

translations.literal: Wang Kejing, chief administrator of Shaoxing Circuit, found the per-capita salt ration inconvenient and had once spoken to the Branch Secretariat, but received no reply. When Kejing became salt commissioner, he convened a meeting wishing to reduce the quota somewhat to relieve the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kejing, chief administrator of Shaoxing, had found the per-capita salt levy burdensome and petitioned the secretariat without reply; when he became salt commissioner he convened a meeting to reduce the quota and ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 沮之者以為有成籍不可改，艮毅然曰：「民實寡而強賦多民之錢，今死、徙已眾矣，顧重改成籍而輕棄民命乎！

translations.literal: Those who obstructed said that established registers could not be changed. Gen said resolutely: "The people are in fact few, yet we forcibly levy much of their money. Now deaths and migrations are already numerous—shall we value preserving the old register and lightly abandon the people's lives!"
translations.idiomatic: Opponents said established registers could not be changed. Gen declared firmly, "The population is shrinking while we force heavy levies; deaths and flight are already numerous—shall we cling to old registers and abandon the people's lives?"

sentences.zh: 且浙右之郡，商賈輻輳，未嘗以口計也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the prefectures of western Zhejiang are thronged with merchants and have never been reckoned by population.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, western Zhejiang is crowded with merchants and has never been taxed by head count.

sentences.zh: 移其所賦，散於商旅之所聚，實為良法。

translations.literal: Shifting the levy and spreading it where travelers and merchants gather is truly a good method.
translations.idiomatic: Shifting the levy to where merchants and travelers congregate is truly the better method.

sentences.zh: 」於是議歲減紹興食鹽五千六百引。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was agreed to reduce Shaoxing's annual salt quota by five thousand six hundred yin.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly agreed to cut Shaoxing's annual salt quota by five thousand six hundred yin.

sentences.zh: 尋有復排前議者，艮欲辭職去，丞相聞之，亟遣留艮，而議遂定。

translations.literal: Soon there were those who revived the earlier proposal; Gen wished to resign and leave. When the chancellor heard of it, he urgently sent orders to retain Gen, and the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When opponents revived the old plan, Gen threatened to resign; the chancellor heard and urgently ordered him retained, and the reform stood.

sentences.zh: 遷海道漕運都萬戶府經歷。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be intendant of the Maritime Grain Transport Ten-Thousand-Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to intendant of the maritime grain transport office.

sentences.zh: 紹興之官糧入海運者十萬石，城距海十八里，歲令有司拘民船以備短送，吏胥得併緣以虐民。

translations.literal: Shaoxing's official grain entering maritime transport was one hundred thousand shi; the city was eighteen li from the sea. Every year officials were ordered to requisition civilian boats for short-distance transport, and clerks seized the opportunity to oppress the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing sent one hundred thousand shi of official grain by sea; the city lay eighteen li inland, and each year officials requisitioned civilian boats for the short haul—giving clerks a chance to abuse the people.

sentences.zh: 及至海次，主運者又不即受，有折缺之患。

translations.literal: When they reached the seashore, those in charge of transport did not immediately accept delivery, and there was the risk of shortage and loss.
translations.idiomatic: At the coast the transport officers did not accept delivery promptly, inviting shortages and losses.

sentences.zh: 艮執言曰：「運戶既有官賦之直，何復為是紛紛也！

translations.literal: Gen insisted: "The transport households already receive the official payment for grain—why all this turmoil!"
translations.idiomatic: Gen insisted, "Transport households already receive official payment for the grain—why all this turmoil?"

sentences.zh: 」乃責運戶自載糧入運船。

translations.literal: He then required the transport households themselves to load the grain onto the transport ships.
translations.idiomatic: He required transport households to load the grain onto the ships themselves.

sentences.zh: 運船為風所敗者，當核實除其數，移文往返，連數歲不絕，艮取吏牘披閱，即除其糧五萬二千八百石、鈔二百五十萬緡，運戶乃免於破家。

translations.literal: When transport ships were wrecked by wind, the amounts should be verified and deducted; documents went back and forth for several years without end. Gen took the clerical records and reviewed them, immediately deducting fifty-two thousand eight hundred shi of grain and two million five hundred thousand strings of paper money; the transport households were thereby spared bankruptcy.
translations.idiomatic: Ships wrecked by wind should have their quotas reduced, but documents shuttled back and forth for years; Gen reviewed the files and at once remitted fifty-two thousand eight hundred shi and two and a half million strings in paper money, sparing transport households from ruin.

sentences.zh: 遷江浙行省檢校官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be auditing officer of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to auditing officer of the Jiang-Zhe secretariat.

sentences.zh: 有詣中書訴松江富民包隱田土，為糧一百七十餘萬石；

translations.literal: Someone went to the Central Secretariat to sue wealthy men of Songjiang for concealing land, amounting to more than 1.7 million shi of grain tax;
translations.idiomatic: Someone petitioned the Central Secretariat claiming Songjiang's wealthy had concealed land worth more than 1.7 million shi in grain tax;

sentences.zh: 沙盪，為鈔五百餘萬緡；

translations.literal: sand flats, amounting to more than five million strings of paper money;
translations.idiomatic: and sand flats worth more than five million strings in paper money;

sentences.zh: 宜立官府糾察收追之。

translations.literal: and proposed that an office be established to investigate and recover these.
translations.idiomatic: and urged establishing an office to investigate and recover them.

sentences.zh: 中書移行省議，遣官驗視，而鬆江獨當十九。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat referred the matter to the Branch Secretariat for discussion and sent officials to inspect; Songjiang alone bore nineteen tenths of the burden.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Secretariat referred the matter to the secretariat for inspection; Songjiang alone bore nine-tenths of the burden.

sentences.zh: 艮至松江，條陳曲折，以破其誑妄，言其「不過欲竦朝廷之聽而報宿怨，且冀創立衙門，為徼名爵計耳。

translations.literal: When Gen reached Songjiang, he laid out the twists and turns in detail to expose the deception, saying: "This is nothing but an attempt to startle the court's attention and settle old grudges, and moreover to hope for establishing a new office as a scheme to seek fame and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Gen reached Songjiang, laid out the facts in detail, and exposed the fraud: "This is only meant to alarm the court, settle old scores, and win a new office for fame and promotion."

sentences.zh: 萬一民心動搖，患生不測，豈國家培養根本之策哉！

translations.literal: If by chance popular sentiment is shaken and unforeseen troubles arise, how is this the state's policy for nurturing its foundation!"
translations.idiomatic: If popular sentiment is shaken and unforeseen trouble follows, how does that serve the state's policy of nurturing its foundation?"

sentences.zh: 」艮言上，事遂寢。

translations.literal: When Gen's memorial went up, the affair was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Gen's memorial went up and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 除江西行省左右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director in the left and right bureaus of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director in the Jiangxi secretariat's left and right bureaus.

sentences.zh: 吉之安福有小吏，誣民欺隱詭寄田租​​九千餘石，初止八家，前後數十年，株連至千家，行省數遣官按問，吏已伏其虛誑，而有司喜功生事者，复勒其民報合徵糧六百餘石，憲司援詔條革去，終莫能止。

translations.literal: In Anfu of Ji there was a petty clerk who falsely accused the people of concealing and fraudulently registering land tax of more than nine thousand shi; at first only eight households were involved, but over several decades the case implicated up to a thousand households. The Branch Secretariat repeatedly sent officials to investigate; the clerk had already confessed to the falsehood, yet officials who delighted in achievements and stirred up affairs again compelled the people to report a combined levy of more than six hundred shi of grain. The surveillance commission cited an imperial regulation to abolish it, but in the end could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: In Anfu, Ji, a clerk falsely accused people of concealing more than nine thousand shi in land tax; what began with eight households spread over decades to a thousand. The secretariat sent investigators repeatedly; the clerk had confessed the fraud, yet ambitious officials still pressed for six hundred more shi; the surveillance commission cited an edict to cancel it but could not stop the demand.

sentences.zh: 艮到官，首言：「是州之糧，比元經理已增一千一百餘石，豈復有欺隱詭寄者乎？

translations.literal: When Gen took office, he spoke first: "This prefecture's grain quota, compared with the Yuan land survey, has already increased by more than eleven hundred shi—how could there still be concealment and fraudulent registration?"
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Gen said at once, "This prefecture's grain quota has already risen more than eleven hundred shi since the Yuan land survey—how can there still be concealed land?"

sentences.zh: 準憲司所擬可也。

translations.literal: The surveillance commission's proposal may be approved."
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commission's proposal should stand."

sentences.zh: 」行省用艮言，悉蠲之。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat adopted Gen's words and remitted the levies entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat followed Gen's advice and remitted the levies entirely.

sentences.zh: 艮在任歲餘，以中憲大夫、淮東道宣慰副使致仕。

translations.literal: After more than a year in office, Gen retired with the titles Grand Master of the Palace and vice commissioner of the Huaidong Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After a year in office he retired as Grand Master of the Palace and vice commissioner of the Huaidong Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 盧琦，字希韓，惠安人，登至正二年進士第。

translations.literal: Lu Qi, styled Xihan, was a native of Hui'an and passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi, courtesy name Xihan, was from Hui'an and took his jinshi degree in 1342.

sentences.zh: 十二年，稍遷至永春縣尹。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was gradually promoted to magistrate of Yongchun County.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was gradually promoted to magistrate of Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 始至，賑饑饉，止橫斂，均賦役，減口鹽一百餘引，蠲包銀榷鐵之無徵者。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, he relieved famine, stopped illegal levies, equalized taxes and corvée, reduced the per-capita salt quota by more than a hundred yin, and remitted uncollected package silver and iron monopoly dues.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he relieved famine, stopped illegal exactions, equalized taxes and labor, cut the per-capita salt quota by more than a hundred yin, and remitted uncollected package silver and iron monopoly dues.

sentences.zh: 已而訟息民安，乃新學宮，延師儒課子弟，月書季考，文風翕然。

translations.literal: Before long litigation ceased and the people were at peace; he then rebuilt the school, invited Confucian teachers to instruct the young, held monthly compositions and quarterly examinations, and literary culture flourished harmoniously.
translations.idiomatic: Soon lawsuits ceased and the people were at peace; he rebuilt the school, brought in Confucian teachers, held monthly essays and quarterly exams, and learning flourished.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑仙遊盜發，琦適在邑境，盜遙見之，迎拜曰：「此永春大夫也。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in the neighboring county of Xianyou; Qi happened to be within the county border. The bandits saw him from afar, came forward and bowed, saying: "This is the great officer of Yongchun."
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose in neighboring Xianyou; Qi happened to be at the border. Seeing him from afar they came forward and bowed, saying, "This is the magistrate of Yongchun."

sentences.zh: 為大夫百姓者，何幸之大乎！

translations.literal: To be the people of such a great officer—what great fortune!
translations.idiomatic: What fortune to be subjects of such a magistrate!

sentences.zh: 吾邑長乃以暴毒驅我，故至此耳。

translations.literal: Our county chief drove us here with cruelty and oppression—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Our county chief drove us here with cruelty—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」琦因立馬喻以禍福，眾皆投刃槊，請縛其酋以自新，琦許之。

translations.literal: Qi thereupon halted his horse and explained fortune and calamity to them; all cast down swords and spears and asked to bind their chief to renew themselves; Qi consented.
translations.idiomatic: Qi reined in his horse and spoke of reward and ruin; they all cast down their weapons and asked to bind their leader and submit; Qi agreed.

sentences.zh: 酋至，琦械送帥府，自是威惠行於境外。

translations.literal: When the chief arrived, Qi sent him in fetters to the marshal's headquarters; from then on his authority and kindness extended beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief came, Qi sent him in chains to the marshal's headquarters; thereafter his authority and kindness extended beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 十三年，泉郡大饑，死者相枕籍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Quan Prefecture suffered great famine; the dead lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Quan prefecture suffered famine; the dead lay piled one upon another.

sentences.zh: 其能行者，皆老幼扶攜，就食永春。

translations.literal: Those who could walk, old and young supporting one another, came to Yongchun for food.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could still walk, old and young together, came to Yongchun for food.

sentences.zh: 琦命分諸浮屠及大家使食之，所存活不可勝計。

translations.literal: Qi ordered distribution among the Buddhist monasteries and great households to feed them; the number saved was beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Qi ordered monasteries and wealthy households to feed them; the lives saved were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 十四年，安溪寇數万人來襲永春。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year bandits from Anxi, tens of thousands strong, came to attack Yongchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year tens of thousands of bandits from Anxi attacked Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 琦聞，召邑民喻之曰：「汝等能戰則與之戰，不能，則我當獨死之爾。

translations.literal: When Qi heard of it, he summoned the county people and told them: "If you can fight, then fight with them; if not, then I alone shall die for you."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Qi summoned the people and said, "If you can fight, fight with me; if not, I alone will die for you."

sentences.zh: 」眾皆感憤，曰：「使君何言也！

translations.literal: All were moved and indignant, saying: "My lord, what words are these!
translations.idiomatic: All were stirred and indignant, crying, "My lord, what words are these!

sentences.zh: 使君父母，我民赤子，其忍以父母畀賊邪！

translations.literal: My lord is parent to us; we are your children—how could we bear to hand our parent over to bandits!
translations.idiomatic: You are our parent and we your children—how could we hand our parent over to bandits!

sentences.zh: 且彼寇方將虜掠我妻子，焚毀我室廬，乃一邑深仇也。

translations.literal: Moreover, those bandits are about to seize our wives and children and burn our houses—they are the deep enemy of our whole county.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, those bandits would seize our wives and children and burn our homes—they are the county's mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，有進無退，使君其勿以為憂。

translations.literal: In today's affair there is advance but no retreat—my lord, please do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Today we advance and do not retreat—my lord, do not worry."

sentences.zh: 」因踴躍爭奮。

translations.literal: Thereupon they leaped up and strove to outdo one another in zeal.
translations.idiomatic: They leaped up, each striving to outdo the other in zeal.

sentences.zh: 琦率以攻賊，大破之。

translations.literal: Qi led them to attack the bandits and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Qi led them against the bandits and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊复傾巢而至，又破之。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits came again in full force and were again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the bandits returned in full force and were defeated again.

sentences.zh: 大小三十餘戰，斬獲一千二百餘人，而邑民無死傷者。

translations.literal: In more than thirty battles large and small, more than twelve hundred were killed or captured, yet among the county people there were none dead or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: In more than thirty engagements they killed or captured over twelve hundred bandits, yet not one townsman was killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 賊大衄，遂遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits suffered a great rout and then fled.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits suffered a crushing defeat and fled.

sentences.zh: 時兵革四起，列郡皆洶洶不寧，獨永春晏然，無異承平時。

translations.literal: At the time warfare rose on every side and every prefecture was turbulent and unsettled; Yongchun alone was peaceful, no different from times of great tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: War flared everywhere and every prefecture was in turmoil; Yongchun alone remained peaceful, as calm as in the best years of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 十六年，改調寧德縣尹而去。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to be magistrate of Ningde County and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to magistrate of Ningde and left Yongchun.

sentences.zh: 鄒伯顏，字從吉，高唐人。

translations.literal: Zou Boyan, styled Congji, was a native of Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Boyan, courtesy name Congji, was from Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 為建寧崇安縣尹。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Chong'an County in Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Chong'an in Jianning.

sentences.zh: 崇安之為邑，區別其土田，名之曰都者五十，五十都之田上送官者，為糧六千石。

translations.literal: As a district, Chong'an divided its land into units called du, fifty in all; grain from the fields of the fifty du submitted to the government amounted to six thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Chong'an divided its land into fifty units called du; grain tax from all fifty du totaled six thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 其大家以五十餘家，而兼五千石；

translations.literal: Great households, more than fifty families, together bore five thousand shi;
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty great households together bore five thousand shi;

sentences.zh: 細民以四百餘家，而合一千石。

translations.literal: humble households, more than four hundred families, combined for one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: more than four hundred humble households combined for one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 大家之田，連跨數都，而細民之糧，或僅升合。

translations.literal: The fields of great households stretched across several du, while the grain tax of humble folk might be only a sheng or he.
translations.idiomatic: Great families' fields spanned several du, while humble folk might owe only a sheng or two.

sentences.zh: 有司常以四百之細民，配五十大家之役，故貧者受役旬日，而家已破。

translations.literal: Officials constantly assigned corvée from the four hundred humble households to match the fifty great households' obligations, so the poor endured labor for ten days and their families were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Officials routinely assigned corvée from four hundred poor households to cover fifty wealthy ones' obligations, so the poor labored ten days and their families were ruined.

sentences.zh: 伯顏曰：「貧弱之受困，一至此乎！

translations.literal: Boyan said: "The distress of the poor and weak has come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Boyan said, "The poor have been driven to this pass!"

sentences.zh: 」乃取其糧籍而分計從，有糧一石者，受一石之役，有糧升斗者，受升斗之役。

translations.literal: He then took the grain registers and divided and calculated obligations accordingly: those with one shi of grain bore one shi's labor; those with sheng or dou bore sheng or dou's labor.
translations.idiomatic: He took the tax registers and apportioned labor by grain owed: one shi of grain meant one shi's labor, a sheng or dou meant a sheng or dou's labor.

sentences.zh: 田多者受數都之役而不可辭，田少者稱其所出而無倖免。

translations.literal: Those with much land bore corvée for several du and could not decline; those with little land reported what they owed and had no escape.
translations.idiomatic: Those with much land bore corvée across several du and could not refuse; those with little paid what they owed and could not evade it.

sentences.zh: 貧因無告之民，始得以休息。

translations.literal: The poor people who had no recourse were thereby able to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The poor, who had nowhere to turn, were at last able to breathe.

sentences.zh: 崇安賦役之均，遂為四方最。

translations.literal: The equality of Chong'an's levies and corvée became foremost in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Chong'an's fair taxes and labor became the model for the entire region.

sentences.zh: 邑有宋趙抃所鑿溝，溉民田數千畝。

translations.literal: In the county was a canal dug by Zhao Bian of Song, irrigating several thousand mu of the people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: The county had a canal dug by Zhao Bian of the Song, which irrigated several thousand mu of farmland.

sentences.zh: 歲久，溝湮而田廢。

translations.literal: After many years the canal silted up and the fields were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Years passed, the canal silted up, and the fields lay fallow.

sentences.zh: 伯顏修長溝十里，繞楓樹陂，累石以為固，溝悉复抃遺跡，而田為常稔，民賴其利。

translations.literal: Boyan repaired a long canal ten li, winding around Maple Tree Embankment, piled stones to make it firm; the canal fully restored Zhao's vestiges, the fields became regularly fertile, and the people relied on its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan rebuilt a ten-li canal around Maple Tree Embankment, reinforcing it with stone; the canal restored Zhao Bian's work, the fields bore reliably, and the people prospered from it.

sentences.zh: 安慶路嘗得造偽鈔者，遣卒械其囚至崇安，求其黨而執之，囚與卒結謀，望風入良民家肆虐。

translations.literal: Anqing Circuit once captured counterfeiters and sent soldiers to escort the prisoners in fetters to Chong'an to seek and arrest their gang; the prisoners and soldiers plotted together and, seizing opportunities, entered honest people's homes to run riot.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing once caught counterfeiters and sent soldiers to escort the prisoners in chains to Chong'an to round up their gang; prisoners and soldiers conspired to raid peaceful households whenever they could.

sentences.zh: 伯顏捕訊得其狀，即執而歸諸安慶，自是偽造之連逮無濫及崇安者。

translations.literal: Boyan arrested and interrogated them, obtained the facts, immediately seized them and returned them to Anqing; from then on those implicated in counterfeiting did not extend indiscriminately to Chong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan arrested and interrogated them, learned the truth, sent them back to Anqing, and thereafter counterfeiting cases no longer swept up innocent Chong'an people.

sentences.zh: 於是行省帥府、御史憲府咸舉其能。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Branch Secretariat, marshal's headquarters, and censorial surveillance office all recommended his ability.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat, marshal's headquarters, and surveillance commission all recommended him for his ability.

sentences.zh: 選調漳州路判官。

translations.literal: He was selected and transferred to be assistant prefect of Zhangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected and transferred to assistant prefect of Zhangzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 劉秉直，字清臣，大都武清人。

translations.literal: Liu Bingzhi, styled Qingchen, was a native of Wuqing in Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhi, courtesy name Qingchen, was from Wuqing in Dadu.

sentences.zh: 至正八年，來為衛輝路總管​​，平徭役，興教化，敦四民之業，崇五土之利，養鰥寡，恤孤獨。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhizheng he came as chief administrator of Weihui Circuit, equalized corvée, promoted education, encouraged the four occupations, honored the benefits of the five grains, nourished widows and widowers, and comforted the orphaned and alone.
translations.idiomatic: In 1348 he became chief administrator of Weihui, equalized corvée, promoted education, encouraged the four occupations, honored agriculture, and cared for widows, orphans, and the destitute.

sentences.zh: 賊劫汲縣民張聚鈔一千二百錠而殺之，賊不獲，秉直具詞致禱城隍祠，而使人伺於死所，忽有村民阿蓮者，戰怖僕地，具言賊之姓名及所在，乃命尉襲之，果得賊於汴，遂正其罪。

translations.literal: Bandits robbed Zhang Ju of Jixian County of twelve hundred ingots of paper money and killed him; the bandits were not captured. Bingzhi prepared a document and prayed at the City God shrine, then sent men to watch at the place of death. Suddenly a villager named Alian trembled and fell to the ground, fully stating the bandits' names and whereabouts; he then ordered the constable to raid them and indeed captured the bandits at Bian, and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits robbed and killed Zhang Ju of Jixi, taking twelve hundred ingots; the culprits escaped. Bingzhi prayed at the City God shrine and posted men at the murder site; a villager named Alian suddenly collapsed in terror and named the bandits and their hideout; a constable raided them and caught them at Bian, and they were punished by law.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，蟲螟生，民患之，秉直禱於八蜡祠，蟲皆自死。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn locusts and borers appeared and the people suffered; Bingzhi prayed at the Eight Sacrifices shrine and the insects all died of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month locusts and borers appeared; Bingzhi prayed at the Eight Sacrifices shrine and the pests died off.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，人相食，死者過半，秉直出俸米，倡富民分粟，餒者食之，病者與藥，死者與棺以葬。

translations.literal: That year there was great famine; people ate one another and more than half died. Bingzhi gave out his salary grain and urged wealthy families to share grain; the hungry ate, the sick were given medicine, the dead were given coffins for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck; people ate one another and more than half perished. Bingzhi gave his salary grain, urged the wealthy to share theirs, fed the hungry, medicated the sick, and coffined the dead.

sentences.zh: 天不雨，禾且槁，秉直詣城北太行之蒼峪神祠，具詞祈祝，有青蛇蜿蜒而出，觀者異之。

translations.literal: Heaven would not rain and the grain was about to wither; Bingzhi went to the Cangyu Spirit shrine of Mount Taihang north of the city, prepared a document and prayed; a green serpent wound out and the onlookers marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Rain failed and the crops were withering; Bingzhi prayed at the Cangyu shrine on Mount Taihang north of the city; a green serpent emerged, to the wonder of all who saw it.

sentences.zh: 辭神而還，行及數里，雷雨大至。

translations.literal: When he left the shrine and returned, after traveling several li, thunder and rain came in great force.
translations.idiomatic: He left the shrine; within a few li a great thunderstorm broke.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，以親老，去官侍養。

translations.literal: When his term ended, because his parents were old, he left office to serve and support them.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he left office to care for his aging parents.

sentences.zh: 許義夫，碭山人。

translations.literal: Xu Yifu was a native of Dangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yifu was from Dangshan.

sentences.zh: 為夏邑縣尹，每親詣鄉社，教民稼穡。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Xiayi County; every year he personally went to village altars to teach the people agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Xiayi he personally visited village altars each year to teach farming.

sentences.zh: 見民勤謹者，出己俸賞之，怠惰者罰之。

translations.literal: When he saw people diligent and careful he rewarded them from his own salary; the idle and lazy he punished.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded the diligent from his own salary and punished the idle.

sentences.zh: 三年之間，境內豐足。

translations.literal: Within three years the district was abundantly provisioned.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years the district was abundantly supplied.

sentences.zh: 後為封丘縣尹，值至正四年大饑，盜賊群起，抄掠州縣。

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Fengqiu County; during the great famine of the fourth year of Zhizheng, bandits rose in groups and plundered prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as magistrate of Fengqiu during the great famine of 1344, bandits rose in bands and raided the districts.

sentences.zh: 義夫聞賊至近境，乃單馬出郊十里外迎之，見賊數百人，義夫力言：「封丘縣小民貧，皆已驚惶逃竄，幸無入吾境也。

translations.literal: When Yifu heard the bandits had neared the border, he went out alone on horseback ten li beyond the suburbs to meet them; he saw several hundred bandits and spoke forcefully: "Fengqiu is a small county and the people are poor; all are already frightened and fled in panic—please do not enter our territory."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing bandits had neared the border, Yifu rode out alone ten li beyond the suburbs to meet them; facing several hundred men he pleaded, "Fengqiu is small and poor; the people have fled in terror—please do not enter our territory."

sentences.zh: 」言辭願款，賊遂他往。

translations.literal: His words were sincere and earnest, and the bandits went elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: His words were earnest and sincere, and the bandits went elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 封丘之民，得免於難。

translations.literal: The people of Fengqiu were spared the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Fengqiu's people were spared disaster.
